remarks: The two most load-bearing candidate portals for actually filing a Factory License in Nagaland — the Labour Department site (labour.nagaland.gov.in) and the EoDB portal (eodb.nagaland.gov.in) that press reports describe as hosting the state's online factory registration/licensing MIS — could not be verified this session because both fail TLS certificate validation ('unable to get local issuer certificate') on every attempt. This was confirmed to be a genuine server-side incomplete certificate chain rather than a local/proxy artifact: the same curl setup, including an explicit --cacert pointing at the session's trusted CA bundle, successfully verified sibling nagaland.gov.in subdomains (ipr., govtpress., industry.) on the same parent domain. These two portals should be re-checked in a later session/phase once (or if) their certificate chains are fixed, since they are very likely the actual application portals for the Factory License itself.

No official Nagaland-specific 'Factories Rules' gazette notification could be located or verified. The Factories Act, 1948 applies in Nagaland via the Factories (Extension to Kohima, Mokokchung, Zunheboto, Wokha and Phek Districts) Act, 1980 (Nagaland Act No. 5 of 1980), but its only locatable full-text copies (India Code, PRS India) were not independently verifiable this session (see excluded list). Secondary sources (a regulatory-tracking newsletter) describe Nagaland's own Factories Rules as not yet separately framed/notified, with the Labour Department's new online system operating as an interim facilitation mechanism pending that notification — this could not be confirmed against a primary government source this session and should be revisited.

The Nagaland Government e-Gazette archive (govtpress.nagaland.gov.in/egazette-latest/) was verified and is live/current (listing issues through October 2026), but no specific gazette issue was found in it that is confirmed (by its text/title) to be the Factories Rules notification — it is included as the authoritative channel to check for that notification, not as the notification itself.

All verifiedSources entries were individually fetched with curl this session (HTTP 200, with content inspected via pandoc for HTML or pdftotext/`file` for PDFs); no URL was included based on a WebSearch snippet alone.
